column1: # MANUALLY MANAGED - reviewed placements of statically linked VC6 SP3
# runtime code and data. Each row is one COFF section of a pinned archive
# member basename, 1-based COFF section number) at its retail RVA, or a
# compiled pristine zlib object (library `zlib`, member = its object), whose
# code is placed by zlib-map.tsv; `size` is the section's size.
# kind: `code`/`data`/`bss` must agree with the section; `alias` is a
# library COMDAT ICF-folded into a game function (verified, not counted);
# `common` is a linker-allocated COMMON symbol (section 0; the largest
# declaration, library or game, is its size); `thunk` is an import-library
# jump stub (section 0). Rows sharing one RVA are ICF-folded COMDATs whose
# symbols retail references at that address.
# `homm3 verify library-code` re-proves every row on each build: unrelocated
# bytes equal retail (zero for bss/common, which must lie in .data at their
# alignment) and every relocation resolves to its symbol's placed
# definition, import slot, game definition or byte-identical game COMDAT.
# Exact rows count as `library-runtime` (`library-vendor` for zlib), plus
# code fill (the 0xCC run before a row, shorter than its alignment) and data
# fill (zeros exactly from one verified row's end to the next aligned row).
# evidence: `copies=N` the section is byte-identical in N members;
# `member-by-continuity` the member continues its neighbours' link-order run;
# member kept); `member-by-link-order` a COMDAT defined by several members is
# kept from the first linked one; `twin-by-*` a non-COMDAT section identical
# to another member's, chosen by link-order continuity or by the symbol that
# retail code references; `icf` folded with the other rows at this RVA;
# `referenced-by-data` a folded COMDAT that only library data references;
# `placed-by-bytes` a section no relocation reaches, found by its bytes and
# relocations inside its member's link-order window; `placed-by-layout` the
# same for an all-zero section, accepted only as the window's sole candidate;
# alignment places the next contribution; `crt-pointer` a .CRT$ table entry
# COMMON declarations in linked members / game objects.
